results.summary: This design implements basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT) in a Tiny Tapeout project. Inputs a, b, and c are routed to outputs not, and, or. The design is tested by setting inputs and verifying outputs. It uses Wokwi and serves as an educational example, but provides minimal documentation.

This design implements several logic gates (AND, NOR, XOR, NOT) in a Tiny Tapeout project. The gates are interconnected between inputs and outputs. It is tested by applying input combinations and observing outputs. The design is intended to drive a 7-segment display to show the letter 'm', but documentation is sparse and the test table is incomplete.

This design uses NOT gates to drive a 7-segment display to show the letter 'A'. It has eight inputs and eight outputs, with outputs mapping to segments. To test, set inputs a-g to 0 and observe outputs turning on. External hardware includes a 7-segment display. The project is educational and created with Wokwi.

This design demonstrates how NAND gates can be configured to produce OR logic. It includes two circuits: one using NAND gates and one using an OR gate, with inputs IN0-IN3 and outputs OUT0-OUT1. Testing involves applying inputs and checking outputs. No external hardware is mentioned, and the project is educational, created with Wokwi.

This design implements a D-type flip-flop. It has inputs IN0 and IN2, and an output to a 7-segment display. The description states that if IN0 and IN3 are on, an output turns on, but IN3 is not listed in the pins. Testing involves setting inputs and observing the output. The project is created with Wokwi and lacks clear documentation.

This design uses XOR and NXOR gates to display the letter 'Z' on a 7-segment display when a specific 8-bit code is entered. Inputs include clock, reset, and direction switches. To test, toggle switches in the sequence on, off, on, on, on, off, on, off. External hardware is a 7-segment display. The project is created with Wokwi and is educational.

This design accepts an 8-bit input and displays its decimal value on a 7-segment display. The description is minimal and the implementation is unclear. It is tested by activating one input at a time. External hardware is a 7-segment display. The project is a first Wokwi design and lacks detailed documentation.

This design implements a 3-bit binary counter that lights up specific horizontal lines on a 7-segment display based on the input value. Inputs 0-7 correspond to binary representations, and outputs drive the display segments. Testing involves setting inputs and observing the illuminated lines. External hardware is a 7-segment display. The project is created with Wokwi and serves as an educational example.

This project has no meaningful documentation. The title and description are placeholders, and the pins are generically named. It is unclear what the design does or how it is tested. External hardware is not specified. The project appears to be an incomplete or template design created with Wokwi.

This design uses combinations of logic gates (AND, NOT, XOR, OR) to produce different patterns on a 7-segment display. A specific input combination (23568) displays the letter 'g'. Testing involves changing input combinations to see different shapes. External hardware may be needed but is not specified. The project is created with Wokwi and is educational.
